data.long_meaning: Ahaz means 'father of awe' in Hebrew. In the Bible, Ahaz was a king of Judah who did not trust in the Lord and led the people away from God. Despite his disobedience, God still showed Ahaz mercy and provided him with a son who would reign in his place. The name Ahaz carries the meaning “None or N/A” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Ahaz usually hope their child will grow to embody none or n/a and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: אחז
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אחז הוא שם עברי שפירושו 'הוא אחז' או 'הוא תפס' או 'ה' אחז'. השם מורכב משתי מילים: 'אח' שפירושו 'אחז' או 'תפס', ו'ז' שפירושו 'הוא' או 'אלוהים'. השם אחז היה שמו של מלך יהודה השישי, שמלך מ-767 עד 735 לפנה"ס. הוא היה בנו של יותם ועליו מסופר בספר מלכים ב', פרקים טז-יח.

in_greek.name: Αχάζ
in_greek.long_meaning: Αχάζ ἦν ὄνομα ἑβραϊκόν, ὃ σημαίνει 'Αὐτός ἔλαβεν' ἤ 'Κύριος ἔλαβεν'. Τὸ ὄνομα Αχάζ προέρχεται ἀπὸ τὸ εβραϊκό ρίζωμα 'אחז', ὃ σημαίνει 'λαβή' ἤ 'κατάσχεσις'. Ὁ Αχάζ ἦν βασιλεὺς τῆς Ιουδαίας, υἱὸς τοῦ Ιωθάμ, καὶ ἐβασίλευσε ἀπὸ τὸ 767 ἕως τὸ 735 π.Χ.

in_latin.name: Achaz
in_latin.long_meaning: Achaz nomen hebraicum est, quod significat 'ipse tenuit' vel 'Dominus tenuit'. Nomen Achaz derivatur a radice hebraica 'אחז', quae significat 'tenere' vel 'capere'. Achaz fuit rex Iudaeae, filius Iotham, et regnavit ab anno 767 usque ad annum 735 ante Christum.

in_english.name: Ahaz
in_english.meaning: He holds or seizes, strong and steadfast
in_english.long_meaning: The name Ahaz originates from the Hebrew root 'אחז' (akhoz), meaning 'to hold' or 'to seize'. Ahaz was the sixth king of Judah, reigning from 767 to 735 BCE. He was the son of Jotham and is mentioned in 2 Kings 16-18. The name Ahaz signifies strength, stability, and divine support, reflecting his royal lineage and spiritual heritage. Throughout Christian tradition, Ahaz represents leadership and faith.

data.cultural_impact: Ahaz is mentioned in both the Old and New Testaments of the Bible, and his story has influenced Jewish and Christian historical, theological, and artistic interpretations. He is remembered as one of the less-than-ideal kings of Judah, and his reign is a reminder of the consequences of disobedience and idolatry.
data.spiritual_significance: Despite his shortcomings, Ahaz is a reminder of God's mercy and faithfulness. Even when a leader strays from the path of righteousness, God still provides a way forward through His grace and providence. Ahaz's story underscores the importance of trusting in God, even when we may not feel that we deserve His mercy. It serves as a reminder that no one is beyond the reach of God's love and forgiveness.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ahaz: In Hebrew, meaning "no brother," symbolizing a sense of isolation or loneliness in one's spiritual journey. In the Christian context, it can represent the call to deepen one's relationship with God in times of solitude and hardship.

biblical_reference.note: Ahaz was a king of Judah, son of Jotham, and reigned from 767 to 735 BCE.

historical_references.reference: Ahaz was a king of Judah who reigned from 735-715 BCE and is known for his idolatrous practices, including allowing the Assyrian king Hezekiah to be taken captive and installing a pagan altar in the Temple in Jerusalem.
historical_references.context: During the Assyrian threat to Judah, Ahaz sought the help of the Assyrian king Tiglath-Pileser III but also turned to idolatrous practices to secure his rule.

historical_references.reference: Ahaz is also remembered for commissioning the construction of a new royal palace in Jerusalem, the first major building project in the city since Solomon's Temple.
historical_references.context: During his reign, Ahaz oversaw the construction of a new royal palace in Jerusalem, which was a significant architectural achievement for the time.
